sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:112832
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 13264 of 2024

Applicant :- Rajeev
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Rakesh Kumar Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Rakesh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Pradeep Kumar,
learned Aga for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime
No. 44 of 2024, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B Ipc and Section 4/10 U.P. Public
Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 1982, Police Station Shahzadnagar, District Rampur
during pendency of the trial.

Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 1982
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that as per allegation in place of applicant another accused appeared in the examination but entire allegation is false and baseless.
4. He further submits that applicant never instructed co-accused Dileep to appear in the examination in his place.
He further submits that it appears that due to some confusion co-accuse Dileep was arrested and it was alleged that he appeared in the examination in place of the applicant.

5. He further submits that except one case which relates to minor offence applicant is not having any previous criminal history.
6. He further submits that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I class and applicant is in jail since 28.02.2024 i.e. for almost five months.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I class and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 28.02.2024 i.e. for almost five months.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. However, there is allegation that in place of the applicant in the examination some other person appeared but all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I class and applicant is in jail since 28.02.2024 i.e. for almost five months.
10.
Further, however, apart from the present case applicant is having criminal history of one another case but that case relates to minor offences.

11. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant - Rajeev be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
14. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

15. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
